topicName: Azure Storage Accounts, Tiers, and Redundancy (LRS, GRS, ZRS)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Azure Storage Accounts, Tiers, and Redundancy"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Storage is Microsoft's cloud storage solution for modern data storage scenarios. A storage account provides a unique namespace in Azure for your data, accessible from anywhere in the world over HTTP or HTTPS."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Storage Account Types"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Standard General Purpose v2 (GPv2): Recommended for most scenarios, supporting blobs, files, queues, and tables."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Premium Block Blobs: High-performance storage optimized for high transaction rates or workloads with large amounts of small objects."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Azure Files Premium: High-performance file shares optimized for enterprise or high-performance computing (HPC) workloads."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Azure Storage Tiers"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure offers different access tiers to store block blob data at the most cost-effective price based on how frequently the data is accessed."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Hot Tier: Optimized for storing data that is accessed frequently. It has higher storage costs but lower access costs."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cool Tier: Optimized for storing data that is infrequently accessed and stored for at least 30 days. Lower storage costs, higher access costs."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Archive Tier: Optimized for data that is rarely accessed and stored for at least 180 days with flexible latency requirements. Lowest storage cost, highest retrieval cost and latency."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Redundancy Options (LRS, ZRS, GRS)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Storage always stores multiple copies of your data so that it is protected from planned and unplanned events, including transient hardware failures, network or power outages, and massive natural disasters."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Locally Redundant Storage (LRS): Copies your data synchronously three times within a single physical location in the primary region. It is the lowest-cost redundancy option."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Zone-Redundant Storage (ZRS): Copies your data synchronously across three Azure availability zones in the primary region."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Geo-Redundant Storage (GRS): Copies your data synchronously three times in the primary region using LRS, and then copies your data asynchronously to a single physical location in the secondary region."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating an Azure Storage Account via Azure CLI"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example of how to create a standard general-purpose v2 storage account with ZRS redundancy using the Azure CLI."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"az storage account create --name mystorageaccount --resource-group MyResourceGroup --location eastus --sku Standard_ZRS --kind StorageV2 --access-tier Hot"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing the right combination of account type, tier, and redundancy ensures high availability, durability, and cost optimization for your cloud architecture."}]
